newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Metals - Aluminium prices slide with demand.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Metals - Aluminium prices slide with demand.

text.p: Taiwan aluminium ingots prices fell to T$47.50 per kilogram from T$49.00 two weeks ago as buyers anticipated a decrease in demand from the construction sector in coming weeks, local metals traders said on Tuesday.
"Buyers expect the construction sector's aluminium demand to fall after its recent peak in March," a metal trader said.

Demand for aluminium ingots had risen in March as construction firms launched advertisement campaigns to promote residential building projects worth some T$200 billion, hoping to lure buyers during the March 29-30 and April 4-6 holidays.

Taiwan traders had predicted that demand for basic metals would pick up slowly as the government's economy stimulus plans took effect on the construction industry, which remained Taiwan's top sector for basic metals consumption.

Loans extended by Taiwan banks to construction firms fell 9.99 percent to T$392.833 billion in February from a year ago, marking the 21st consecutive month of declines, Taiwan central bank figures showed.
Banks have been particularly cautious in granting loans to firms in the construction sector, which has been in deep recession since the local property market peaked in 1989.
Taiwan's interior ministry said in late March it was arranging T$61.477 billion in credits from the cabinet's Medium and Long-term Funds to offer low-cost loans for first-time homebuyers.
